body:
`language::rust_refs.ImportSite` holds no attributes (its fields are `local`, `path`, `range`, `alias`, `outside`, `glob`). So when extract carries a gated import such as `#[cfg(feature = "x")]`, `#[cfg(test)]`, `#[cfg(unix)]` or `#[allow(...)] use ...;`, the new module gets it as an unconditional import. In a normal build that import can name a module that does not exist, and the build breaks.

Fix: keep the import's outer attributes when it is carried. Either store the attribute text on the site when it is collected, or recover it from the originating header or `use` symbol; the agent picks whichever fits the code.

Test: a feature- or test-gated module with a matching gated import, and a moved item under the same gate. After extract, the carried import in the target still has its attribute, and the normal (ungated) build compiles.

Touches the same function as task:c970ab48b3b62497 (`extract::rust.carry_imports`), so it runs after it.
title: extract: carried imports keep their attributes
